Veteran Nigerian actor and broadcaster, Chief Pete Edochie, has died at the age of 79. Edochie died at 12:30am on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, in Enugu, after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. His death was announced in a statement signed by his son, Leo Pete Edochie, on behalf of the family and shared on Instagram on Wednesday. The statement described the deceased as a beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman, adding that he hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, Anambra State. The statement read, “With profound sadness and hearts bowed in total submission to the will of Almighty God,we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman, Chief Dr Pete EDOCHIE, MON (Ononenyi) a retired broadcaster and veteran sctor, who departed this life on Wednesday,25th November 2026 at 12.30am after a protracted battle with prostate cancer in Enugu, Nigeria. Chief Leo Pete EDOCHIE For the Family” Pete Edochie: Life, career and legacy of a Nollywood legend Catholic diocese advises candidates on peace, tolerance APGA senatorial candidate, NDC lawmaker clash Edochie was one of Nigeria’s most recognisable actors, renowned for his commanding screen presence and portrayal of traditional patriarchal figures. He rose to national and international prominence for his role as Okonkwo in the 1987 Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s novel, Things Fall Apart. His performance in the television adaptation established him as a prominent figure in Nigerian acting and helped introduce his work to audiences beyond the country. Before becoming widely known as an actor, Edochie had a career in broadcasting. He began working as a broadcaster in 1967 before transitioning into acting, where he built a career spanning several decades and featured in numerous Nigerian films. His contributions to the entertainment industry earned him the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON).
